cancer_indication: Extended adjuvant therapy for early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer following adjuvant trastuzumab; and (with capecitabine) for metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer after ≥2 prior anti-HER2 regimens.
moa: Neratinib is an irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor that covalently binds and inhibits EGFR, ERBB2 (HER2), and ERBB4 (HER4), preventing receptor autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways. In human breast-cancer models and clinical contexts, this blockade suppresses proliferative and survival signaling and promotes apoptosis and cell-cycle arrest. In ER+/HER2+ disease, neratinib is described as complementing endocrine therapy, with clinical activity reported for combinations such as neratinib with fulvestrant and trastuzumab in ER+ metastatic disease with ERBB2 mutations.

REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2.description: HER2/ERBB2 receptor tyrosine-kinase signaling that drives downstream proliferative and survival cascades.
REACTOME_SIGNALING_BY_ERBB2.interpretation: ERBB2 pathway activity is a core oncogenic dependency in HER2-driven breast cancer and is a key axis targeted by neratinib.

REACTOME_MAPK1_MAPK3_SIGNALING.description: MAPK1/MAPK3 (ERK1/2) signaling downstream of activated receptor tyrosine kinases controlling proliferation and survival programs.
REACTOME_MAPK1_MAPK3_SIGNALING.interpretation: MAPK/ERK output is a major downstream effector of EGFR/HER2 signaling in breast cancer and is part of the growth circuitry impacted by ERBB blockade.

REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING_IN_CANCER.description: PI3K–AKT signaling controlling cell survival and growth, frequently dysregulated in cancer via pathway alterations.
REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING_IN_CANCER.interpretation: PI3K/AKT activity supports tumor survival and is highlighted as both a downstream node of HER signaling and a pathway that can shape response or escape to HER2-directed therapy in breast cancer.

HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.description: mTORC1-driven anabolic growth and translation programs that integrate nutrient and growth-factor signals.
HALLMARK_MTORC1_SIGNALING.interpretation: mTORC1 signaling reflects tumor growth-state control downstream of AKT and is described as a relevant survival/growth axis in the neratinib mechanism and resistance context.

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: E2F-regulated transcriptional program linked to G1/S progression and proliferative cell-cycle activity.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation: E2F-target activity captures proliferative drive and cell-cycle progression, which is discussed as changing with effective ERBB blockade and as a potential bypass route when sustained.

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Core apoptotic machinery and pro-death signaling programs that execute programmed cell death.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Apoptosis is a key tumor-control outcome described with HER-family signaling inhibition, reflecting a shift away from survival signaling in responsive settings.

HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.description: Estrogen receptor (ER)-linked transcriptional program reflecting sustained/late ER-driven gene expression.
HALLMARK_ESTROGEN_RESPONSE_LATE.interpretation: ER signaling is described as clinically relevant in HR+ breast cancer subtypes where cross-talk with HER2 can influence benefit and where combination endocrine strategies are discussed alongside neratinib.

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Higher HER2 dependence (amplification/overexpression or activating ERBB2 context as described) is presented as a setting where neratinib’s direct ERBB2 inhibition is most effective.
PIK3CA alterations are explicitly described as being associated with enhanced benefit from neratinib in ExteNET (noted as counterintuitive in the source).

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Upregulated PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling driven by PIK3CA mutation is described as a bypass survival mechanism that can reduce neratinib efficacy when the pathway remains high.
Upregulation of alternate tyrosine-kinase signaling via ERBB3 is described as a mechanism to reactivate AKT/MAPK and bypass HER2 blockade.
Upregulation of IGF1R signaling is described as an alternative receptor input that can restore downstream survival signaling despite ERBB inhibition.
Upregulation of HGF–MET signaling is described as a bypass route to reactivate AKT/MAPK and support resistance to HER2 inhibition.
Elevated Cyclin D1/E2F axis activity (including CCND1 amplification as stated) is described as enabling proliferation and overcoming neratinib-induced growth suppression.
Upregulation of Cyclin D1–CDK4 signaling is described as sustaining RB phosphorylation/E2F activation and promoting resistance to neratinib’s antiproliferative effects.
Overexpression of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family signaling is described as a survival mechanism that can blunt neratinib-induced cell death.
TNF-linked inflammatory survival signaling (via TNFα/NFκB framing in the source) is described as a potential escape program under chronic neratinib exposure.
Upregulation of IL6-associated survival signaling (with STAT3 noted) is described as a potential resistance mechanism supporting survival under HER2 inhibition.
STAT3-associated survival signaling is described as part of an inflammatory/pro-survival program that may help cells resist neratinib-induced death.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: PTEN loss is described as hyperactivating PI3K/AKT and mTORC1 signaling, enabling bypass survival signaling and contributing to resistance.
RB1 loss is described as allowing bypass of neratinib’s antiproliferative effects by sustaining E2F-driven proliferation.
Loss or downregulation of p53 function (including TP53 mutation context) is described as limiting apoptotic responses to ERBB2 inhibition and contributing to resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer: Neratinib is approved as extended adjuvant therapy for early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer (following trastuzumab); US indication covers early-stage HER2-overexpressing disease after adjuvant trastuzumab, while EU approval limits it to hormone receptor–positive HER2+ disease.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer: In 2020, the FDA approved neratinib (with capecitabine) for metastatic HER2+ breast cancer after ≥2 prior anti-HER2 regimens.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer w: As of 2023, NCCN advises neratinib use (often with fulvestrant and trastuzumab) in HER2-negative metastatic patients with activating ERBB2 mutations.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.ER+/HER2+ disease: Neratinib may complement endocrine therapy in hormone-receptor–positive subtypes, with greater benefit described in HR+ patients and with combination endocrine blockade (e.g., neratinib, fulvestrant, trastuzumab) reported to yield objective responses in ER+ metastatic disease with ERBB2 mutation context.
